config.title: Auth Context

intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure authentication system for a React app using React Context and TypeScript. You'll learn how to create a centralized Auth Context to manage user login state and share it across components without prop drilling. The core programming concept is React Context API, which allows you to pass data through the component tree without explicitly passing props. You'll use TypeScript to define strict types for authentication data, ensuring type safety and better code reliability. By the end, you'll have a functional context provider that handles user authentication state and provides it to any component in your app.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is a foundational pattern used in virtually every modern web application that requires user authentication. You'll see it in action in dashboards like GitHub or Notion, where the user's login state controls access to private repositories or workspaces, and in e-commerce sites like Amazon, where it manages the shopping cart and personalized recommendations. As a developer, implementing an Auth Context allows you to securely manage user sessions, conditionally render UI elements like navigation menus, and protect routes across your entire application without prop drilling.

objectives: Initialize a React context with TypeScript interfaces for authentication state
Construct a custom provider component that manages authentication logic
Implement a custom hook to consume the authentication context throughout the application
Configure components to conditionally render content based on authentication status
Bind authentication actions (login/logout) to UI event handlers
Update application state in response to authentication events
Integrate the authentication context with multiple components in a React application

steps.title: Import React and useContext
steps.instruction: Import React and the useContext hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useContext from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useContext from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and useContext are added to the file.
successCriteria: React and useContext are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useContext from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create AuthContext interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named AuthContextType with three properties: user (type string | null), login (type (username: string) => void), and logout (type () => void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Remember to include proper TypeScript type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useContext from 'react' here

// Define AuthContextType interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape of your authentication context, including user state and authentication functions.
successCriteria: AuthContextType interface is defined with user (string | null), login (function), and logout (function) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties are defined with the correct TypeScript types: user should be string | null, login should accept a string parameter, and logout should have no parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is incomplete or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword, name it AuthContextType, and include all three properties with proper TypeScript type annotations.

steps.title: Create AuthContext with default values
steps.instruction: Create the AuthContext using React.createContext. Provide default values: user should be null, and login and logout should be placeholder functions that console.log a message.
steps.hint: Use React.createContext and pass an object with the properties defined in your AuthContextType interface as the default value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a context with default values
const ThemeContext = React.createContext({ theme: 'light', toggleTheme: () => console.log('toggle') });
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthContext is created with the correct TypeScript type and default values, ready to be used by the Provider and consumers.
successCriteria: AuthContext is created using React.createContext with an object containing user: null, login: () => console.log('login'), and logout: () => console.log('logout') as default values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're providing all three properties (user, login, logout) with the correct default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthContext wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using React.createContext with an object matching the AuthContextType interface.

steps.title: Create AuthProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthProvider that accepts a children prop and returns AuthContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes children as a prop and returns AuthContext.Provider with children as its content.
steps.expectedOutcome: An AuthProvider component is defined that will wrap the application and provide the auth context.
successCriteria: AuthProvider component is created with children prop and returns AuthContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component accepts children and returns AuthContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. It should be named AuthProvider, accept children, and return AuthContext.Provider.

steps.title: Add user state to AuthProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component, use the useState hook to create a user state variable initialized to null.
steps.hint: Call useState with null as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into a state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of useState for a string state
const [name, setName] = useState<string | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component will have a user state variable managed by useState, ready to be used in the authentication context.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called inside AuthProvider with null as initial value, and the state variable and setter are properly destructured.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState correctly with proper destructuring and initialization to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState inside the AuthProvider component to create a user state variable initialized to null.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component, create a function named 'login' that takes a 'username' parameter of type string and updates the user state with that username.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setUser with the provided username. The function should be defined inside the component to have access to the setUser state setter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now contains a login function that will update the user state when called.
successCriteria: A function named 'login' is defined inside AuthProvider, takes a string parameter 'username', and calls setUser with that username.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the login function takes a 'username' parameter of type string and calls setUser with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function isn't defined correctly. It should be inside AuthProvider, take a string parameter, and update the user state.

steps.title: Provide context value to AuthProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component, return an AuthContext.Provider element that wraps the children prop and passes the context value containing user, login, and logout.
steps.hint: The value prop of AuthContext.Provider should be an object matching the AuthContextType interface. Use the state and handler functions you've already created.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component now returns an AuthContext.Provider that makes the authentication state and handlers available to all child components.
successCriteria: AuthProvider returns AuthContext.Provider with a value prop containing user, login, and logout properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning AuthContext.Provider with the correct value object containing all three properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider isn't set up correctly. Check that you're returning AuthContext.Provider with the proper value prop.

steps.title: Create useAuth custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook named useAuth that returns the value from useContext(AuthContext) with proper typing.
steps.hint: Define a function called useAuth that uses the useContext hook with AuthContext and returns its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useAuth hook is defined and returns the AuthContext value with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The useAuth hook is created, uses useContext with AuthContext, and returns the context value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your useAuth hook uses useContext with AuthContext and returns its value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useAuth hook is not properly defined. It should be a function that calls useContext(AuthContext) and returns the result.

steps.title: Export AuthContext and useAuth
steps.instruction: Export the AuthContext and useAuth custom hook from the module so they can be imported and used in other components.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before the declarations of AuthContext and useAuth, or add export statements at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthContext and useAuth hook are exported and ready to be imported in other components.
successCriteria: AuthContext and useAuth are exported from the module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both AuthContext and useAuth are exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Check that you're exporting both AuthContext and useAuth.
